jobs.excerpt: ABOUT NEW ENERGY NEXUSNew Energy Nexus (NEX) is an international NGO that supports climate solutions and builds a more equitable clean energy economy.
jobs.description:
ABOUT NEW ENERGY NEXUS

New Energy Nexus (NEX) is an international NGO that supports climate solutions and builds a more equitable clean energy economy. Our laser focus is on clean energy entrepreneurs: providing them with funds, accelerators, and networks to thrive. They are our main audience and our agent of change.

We started in California in 2004 and now operate across China, India, Southeast Asia, East and West Africa, and Australia. We have leveraged US$5.4 billion in investment and supported more than 11,000 entrepreneurs.

ABOUT THE ROLE & OPPORTUNITY

The Director of Development Strategy & Operations will lead the internal engine behind New Energy Nexus' global fundraising and business development efforts. Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, this role sits at the center of NEX's development team — turning what our development and partnerships staff and country teams learn on the ground with funders into a coherent, prioritized fundraising strategy, and making sure the team is coordinated, resourced, and focused on the highest-value opportunities.

This is not primarily a donor-facing relationship management role. It is a strategy, team leadership, and fundraising operations role for someone who understands the business and fund development cycle deeply enough to translate frontline intelligence — what funders are signaling, what's landing and what isn't, where proposals are stalling, which markets and programs are attracting interest — into clear direction for where the team should spend its time.

The Director will lead and develop NEX's global platform-level development team, ensuring that individual team members' skills and expertise are deployed effectively against organizational priorities, while bringing together the knowledge and fundraising capabilities of country leaders, chapter teams, and program leads. The ideal candidate has the analytical rigor and systems mindset of a strong operations leader, paired with real fluency in philanthropic and development finance fundraising, so they can be a credible internal leader and partner to a globally distributed team of fundraisers, country directors, and program leads.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Fundraising Strategy & Intelligence (50%)

  • Help develop a living, prioritized development strategy based on proposal outcomes, funder conversations, and market signals gleaned from team conversations and learnings from fundraisers, country directors, and program leads
  • Identify where NEX should be focusing time and effort across programs and geographies, based on funder appetite, pipeline strength, and organizational priorities.
  • Maintain a clear view of the funding pipeline across the network — by funder, program, chapter, and stage — and flag risks, gaps, or unrestricted-vs-restricted balance issues early.
  • Translate strategy into concrete guidance: which opportunities to prioritize, which proposals need repositioning, where the team is over- or under-invested.
  • Serve as a thought partner to the CEO and program leads on funding strategy, drawing on patterns across markets rather than any single relationship.

Team Coordination & Enablement (35%)

  • Lead and develop the global platform-level development team including recruiting, hiring, onboarding, coaching, and managing performance, and ensure team members' skills are effectively leveraged against NEX's development priorities.
  • Translate the development strategy into a clear rolling work plan for the team, aligning ownership, resources, and timelines.
  • Build strong collaboration across the global development function, bringing together the expertise and fundraising capabilities of platform-level staff, country leaders, fundraisers, and program leads to maximize collective impact.
  • Run the operating rhythm of the fundraising team: pipeline reviews, proposal coordination across programs/chapters/finance/communications, and prioritization check-ins.
  • Coordinate multi-country and multi-program proposals, including combining country and program inputs into a cohesive narrative and budget that aligns with broader NEX operational and growth priorities.
  • Build and own a central library of fundraising collateral - pitch decks, one-pagers, case studies, program summaries, impact data - so materials for funder meetings and conference talks can be assembled quickly rather than built from scratch each time.
  • Draft and maintain core funder and conference decks, adapting a standard set of modular slides/content to each audience so our fundraisers can focus their time on external relationship-building and speaking rather than deck production.
  • Partner with the Chief Communications Officer to keep collateral aligned with current messaging, program updates, and brand standards.
  • Provide country leads and fundraisers with the tools, templates, frameworks, and support to raise funds effectively and report consistently.
  • Build feedback loops so that what is learned through funder and country-level engagement consistently makes its way back into strategy, priorities, and team planning.

Systems, Data & Reporting (15%)

  • Accountable for the fundraising CRM and pipeline-tracking systems, ensuring data quality, consistent use across chapters, and useful reporting.
  • Produce regular and ad hoc reporting and dashboards for NEX leadership on pipeline health, funder trends, and progress against platform fundraising goals.
  • Standardize proposal, reporting, and stewardship templates and processes across the global platform-level team.
  • Track outcomes against the fundraising strategy and refine it as new data comes in.
  • Ensure fundraising protocols and internal as well as external reporting are completed on time and to consistent quality standards

SUCCESS IN THE FIRST 6–12 MONTHS

Success in this role will mean building a more coordinated, strategic, and effective global development function. By the end of the first 6–12 months, the Director will have:

  • Established clear visibility into NEX's global fundraising pipeline, priorities, risks, and opportunities, with leadership able to make decisions based on reliable, current information.
  • Built a strong operating rhythm across the global platform-level development team, with clear ownership, effective collaboration, and team members' skills deployed against the highest-priority fundraising opportunities.
  • Improved coordination across platform, country, and program teams so that high-value proposals are prioritized appropriately, developed collaboratively, and submitted on time and at a consistently high quality.
  • Established consistent CRM and pipeline management practices across the development function, with data being used to inform strategy, prioritization, and reporting.
  • Created a well-organized, accessible library of standardized fundraising collateral and tools that enables fundraisers and country teams to move more quickly and consistently.
  • Established effective feedback loops between funder and country-level intelligence, fundraising performance, and the organization's overall development strategy.

Requirements

Professional Experience

  • 8+ years of experience in fundraising, development operations, or a closely related strategy/operations function (e.g., sales operations, revenue operations, or enablement), with at least 5 years touching nonprofit or philanthropic fundraising directly.
  • Demonstrated experience turning frontline or field-level input into strategy and prioritization.
  • Experience managing or closely coordinating a distributed team, including non-direct-report relationships (e.g., chapter or country-based staff).
  • Strong track record with CRM/pipeline systems and translating data into decisions, not just dashboards.
  • Familiarity with the climate, clean energy, or entrepreneurship support landscape is a strong plus.

Personal Attributes

  • Structured, analytical thinker who is comfortable synthesizing messy, qualitative field input into clear recommendations.
  • High level of adaptability in an environment with evolving team structures and workflows, with a genuine comfort operating in ambiguity - this means being a self-starter and embodying a growth mindset.
  • High emotional intelligence — able to lead and support a development team well, build trust with country leads across diverse cultural contexts, and approach unfamiliar markets and norms with genuine curiosity and cultural sensitivity.
  • Exceptional written communication skills — able to distill complex, multi-market fundraising intelligence into concise strategy and proposals.
  • Strong project management skills; able to run a coordination function across concurrent proposals, deadlines, and stakeholders.
  • Comfortable being an internal partner and "connective tissue" role rather than the primary external face of fundraising.
  • Ability to work with a global team across time zones, with periodic travel for internal team meetings and relevant conferences/convenings.
  • Proficiency in database/CRM management, Google Workspace, and Slack.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Foundational knowledge of global clean energy and climate change solutions and ecosystems and willingness to engage in in-depth self-learning on any gaps.
  • Experience building or adding structure to a development operations function from an earlier, more informal stage.
  • Due to the global nature of the organization and team, some meetings will take place outside of regular work hours.

Benefits

BENEFITS AND COMPENSATION

This is a full-time remote position. Relocation assistance is not available for this role and compensation is competitive for the market the candidate is based in. Applicable benefits such as medical, dental, vision, paid time off, paid holidays and insurance will depend on the location of the selected candidate.

TO APPLY, TIMELINE, AND PROCESS

jobs.excerpt: About UsEvery year, millions die from preventable diseases because vital services do not reach them.
jobs.description:
About Us

Every year, millions die from preventable diseases because vital services do not reach them. A root cause is broken data: missing or unreliable IDs, fragmented records, and inflated reporting. Without accurate data on who receives services, governments and NGOs cannot deliver care effectively, track impact, or target life-saving resources.

Simprints is a nonprofit tech company that partners with ministries and funders to verify identities, digitise workflows, and enable evidence-based decisions so the right services reach the right people at the right time. We co-design end-to-end digital solutions with the people who use them, from the frontlines to national dashboards. Our biometric products integrate with health records to drive accuracy, accountability, and insights.

We build for scale with privacy-first, open-source, and cost-effective technology that strengthens national digital public infrastructure. Studies have shown that Simprints increases impact through real-time, precision data, for example, increasing maternal health visits by 38% in Bangladesh or accurate HIV tracing by 62% in Malawi. To date, we’ve worked in over 17 countries, helping deliver health, aid, and finance to over 4 million people.

Our mission is simple: make sure every vaccine, every dollar, and every public good reaches the people who need them most.

About the Role

The Partnerships Operations Manager will help build the operating engine behind Simprints’ growth. This role will support the Partnerships team to identify, qualify, and progress high-value opportunities more effectively, while improving the systems, data, and automation that underpin our revenue generation.

You will sit at the intersection of sales operations, market intelligence, AI-enabled automation, and proposal development. One day you might be improving our CRM and pipeline reporting; the next, building an AI-assisted workflow to scan donor opportunities; the next, coordinating inputs for a grant application or preparing a funder brief.

This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys creating structure, improving processes, and helping senior relationship-holders move faster and more strategically. You will make the Partnerships team sharper, more disciplined, and better equipped to grow a healthy and diversified pipeline.

Job Details

  • Job Title: Partnerships Operations Manager
  • Reporting To: Chief Strategy Officer
  • Grade: UK Grade IC5 - Up to £45,000
  • Location: Remote

Requirements

Key Responsibilities

  1. Manage and improve Partnerships systems and pipeline operations
    Revamp our CRM engine and maintain CRM hygiene, pipeline data, opportunity and task tracking, dashboards, and reporting so the team has clear visibility on priorities, risks, next steps, and revenue forecasts.
  2. Build AI-enabled automation for growth and fundraising workflows
    Design practical automations to support funder scanning, opportunity alerts, donor research, meeting preparation, proposal content development, follow-up tracking, and pipeline reporting.
  3. Scout and qualify new opportunities
    Monitor the market for relevant grants, RFPs, funder calls, innovation challenges, and strategic partnership opportunities, using clear criteria to assess fit, competitiveness, revenue potential, impact, and internal effort required.
  4. Support grant applications and proposal development
    Coordinate timelines, internal inputs, compliance checks, and supporting materials for proposals and funder submissions; draft or refine selected sections where needed.
  5. Strengthen market, funder, and partner intelligence
    Produce concise research outputs such as funder briefs, opportunity summaries, country or sector snapshots, partner maps, and go/no-go recommendations to support better decision-making.

Skills and experience

  1. Must have experience specifically in a mission-driven, technology, global health, or international development context in sales operations, growth operations, fundraising operations, business development operations,
  2. Strong systems and process skills, including experience managing CRMs, pipelines, dashboards, spreadsheets, trackers, or workflow tools.
  3. Confidence using AI and automation tools to improve team efficiency, reduce manual work, and create scalable processes.
  4. Excellent research, analytical, and synthesis skills, with the ability to turn complex market or funder information into clear recommendations.
  5. Strong written communication and project coordination skills, including the ability to support proposals, support and produce presentations, funder briefs, internal decision documents, and cross-team deadlines.

How we work
We confront the grey. We practise transparency and radical candour, listen deeply, share information openly, and speak up when our ethical compass is challenged, so that psychological safety is real and everyone can do their best work.

We leave our egos at the door. We bring curiosity, kindness, and a positive attitude, seek first to understand, and remember to laugh together. We stay humble about our small part in big global problems, and we remain bold about our ambition to drive change.

We find a way. We plan with clear strategies, deliverables, deadlines, and metrics, step out of our comfort zones, and make it happen. When a plan is not working, we learn from the data, adapt quickly, and keep moving in service of the mission.

We remember why we are here. Impact for people comes first. We act like owners, hold ourselves to high standards, and work across teams to close data gaps and increase coverage, so the right services reach the right people at the right time.

We celebrate the differences. We treat every person with compassion, empathy, and respect, build inclusive spaces where diverse perspectives are welcomed, involve people in important decisions, and share credit generously, because our best ideas can come from anywhere.

Benefits

5 Reasons to Join Simprints

Life is short. We believe work should be inspirational, meaningful and fun. At Simprints, we’re taking on global development’s biggest challenges, powered by an amazing culture and incredible people. Work with us, and you will grow faster, learn more, and take on great responsibilities with the potential to make lasting change.

1. Genuine Impact. Work directly with our partners and users to deliver technology that has the potential to impact millions of lives across the globe. At Simprints, you’ll be part of a team that is passionate about driving real change.

2. An incredible, diverse team. Our work is at the intersection of technology and global development, and we’ve managed to build an amazing team drawn from all over the world. But don’t take our word for it—we’re an externally recognised as a Great Place to Work, and a 2025 Best Workplace for Women amonst many other accolades.

3. Mutual Flex. We champion a work culture where autonomy and trust are paramount, steering clear of mere face-time metrics. Whether it's managing life's essentials like healthcare appointments or adapting work hours to match your peak productivity times, we've got you covered. In return, we count on your reciprocal flexibility when mission-critical moments arise, like stepping up for a crucial client discussion on a Friday or tackling unexpected technical glitches beyond regular hours.

4. Ultimate work-life balance.

    1. We offer a 4-day workweek, meaning everybody has the option to have Fridays off.
    2. We also offer unlimited annual leave, which allows you to prioritise your well-being

As long as you're driving results and fostering teamwork, we encourage you to strike that perfect balance between your professional and personal life. Our commitment to this model's success is solidified through semi-annual productivity assessments with our board, ensuring that our high standards of performance are consistently met.

5. Professional development. We promote continual learning and put our money where our mouth is with development plans and access to global experts through the GLG network

We also have a generous professional development budget for each colleague – “Eduprints”. Is there some training you’d like, or maybe you could benefit from professional coaching? Simply provide a business case that shares your aspirations and the resources you need, and we'll do our best to support you.

We care about both your development in Simprints and your holistic long-term career goals. Simprints Alumni have gone on to work for Google, World Bank, Gavi the vaccine alliance, Save the Children, and other top players.

About this role:

Our clients, General Counsel/Chief Legal Officers or the senior-most individuals responsible for Legal responsibilities, amongst others e.g. compliance, audit, and enterprise risk management, find themselves challenged with the pace of change within the Legal function and their respective organizations as companies continue to focus on developing digital dexterity, managing shifting business models and serving evolving customer and workforce expectations. With the support of their Executive Partner, our Gartner for General Counsel (GC) clients more adeptly assess the changes needed within their organization, manage legal and related risks more effectively, achieve their goals more quickly, and operate with a higher assurance of success. As an Executive Partner, you will have the opportunity to deliver solutions for the most critical legal, governance, and risk management challenges facing companies across all industries.

Partnering with our clients means that no two days are the same; you could be supporting the development of the overall legal department strategy and long-term vision, providing recommendations on assessing legal department workload and creating legal metrics and budgets, advising in building or growing the legal operations team to support critical transformation objectives, managing legal talent or restructuring compliance, privacy, enterprise risk or other programs. Clients will also look to you for advice and support on working with the Board, CEO, and the rest of the management team on critical business goals and risks, communicating the value of the legal function, establishing effective governance and oversight processes, as well as staying on top of emerging and top risks to the enterprise. Other emerging priorities include robust third party risk management strategies, coordinated approaches to cyber and information governance, legal technology and AI adoption, and effective reporting and disclosure processes. Gartner for GC Executive Partners (EPs) serve as accountability partners through delivery of Gartner research insights and personal experiences/expertise on key initiatives, priorities, and strategies of their GC clients.

What You’ll Do

  • Provide executive advisory services to GC members who work across all industries and business models.

  • Synthesize Gartner insights and data to deliver world class advisory support through ongoing bi-weekly client engagement and periodic client working sessions. The ability and willingness to operate independently to adapt materials fit for client use is required.

  • Host, facilitate, and/or participate in periodic member activities, including working sessions to develop strategy, peer roundtables, sessions and client meetings at the annual conference and virtual webinars. These activities may be delivered virtually or on-site depending on circumstance.

  • Define and deliver innovative solutions by assessing member needs and developing a customized value plan in accordance with overall Executive Program strategy and product deliverables.

  • Facilitate member interaction and peer collaboration through the Gartner for GC member community portal and assisted member connections.

  • Work as a collaborative Gartner team member serving members in conjunction with Client Support Professionals and Account Executives.

  • Participate in all phases of the member lifecycle: pre-sale, on-boarding, relationship management, delivery, review, and renewal.

  • Whilst you will not be responsible for creating content, you will be partnering with Research Analysts to help identify potential gaps in material that is relevant and valuable to our members.

  • There will be a considerable focus on sales enablement in this role. You are responsible for member retention and for contributing to account growth through direct support of Gartner Sales Associates:

    • Working with the sales teams to help them understand the true value of the Guided Product to the member vs the Self-Directed product.

    • Building their confidence and ability to effectively engage with and sell to this level of C-suite prospect.

    • Through the creation of Value Stories, enable the sales associates to bring the service to life.

    • You will be partnering with sales on account planning / development activities as well as being present in proof-of-concept (POC) engagements with prospective clients.

What You’ll Need

  • The Executive Partner will be an accomplished Corporate General Counsel, working with the C-suite, the Board of Directors and a host of stakeholders, with a broad base of expertise who has operated at a senior leadership level and driven change at all levels. Seeking candidates that have been the GC of public organizations with at least $1B in annual revenue.

  • At least 5+ years of experience working as a GC (or the top most Legal role within an organization) and at least 15+ years of experience in Corporate Legal environments.

  • An in-depth understanding of the Legal function and other adjacent functions, e.g., Compliance, Audit & Risk etc.

  • Ideally with a background across multiple industries to be able to support a wide variety of member organizations.

  • Law Firm experience, including client relationship management and revenue generation activities, is also highly beneficial.

  • Technologically savvy; our model is lean, and you’ll need to handle your own administrative tasks.

  • Proficient in the use of Microsoft Office suite of tools to adapt Power Points, leverage Excel Spreadsheets, and to use Word to draft client-ready materials.

  • Consulting background a plus.

Who You Are

  • Critical thinker and problem solver demonstrating the ability to assess our Member’s situations and provide actionable, outcome-based business/technical advice as well as the ability to leverage appropriate Gartner resources to help Members achieve results.

  • Ability to build strategic internal partnerships with key roles across the organization and positively impact change

  • This role is a Client-facing position that requires a high level of Executive presence and ability to quickly build trust and deliver value.

  • Demonstrate superior verbal and written communication skills as well as strong facilitation and presentation skills. Excellent communication and relationship management skills

  • Willing to work independently and handle administrative tasks.

THIS IS A REMOTE ROLE THAT CAN BE BASED ANYWHERE IN THE UNITED STATES.

Who are we?

At Gartner, Inc. (NYSE:IT), we guide the leaders who shape the world.

Our mission relies on expert analysis and bold ideas to deliver actionable, objective business and technology insights, helping enterprise leaders and their teams succeed with their mission-critical priorities.

Since our founding in 1979, we’ve grown to 20,000 associates globally who support over 13,000 client enterprises in ~90 countries and territories. We do important, interesting and substantive work that matters. That’s why we hire associates with the intellectual curiosity, energy and drive to want to make a difference. The bar is unapologetically high. So is the impact you can have here.

What makes Gartner a great place to work?

Our vast, virtually untapped market potential offers limitless opportunities – opportunities that may not even exist right now – for you to grow professionally and flourish personally. How far you go is driven by your passion and performance.

We hire remarkable people who collaborate and win as a team. Together, our singular, unifying goal is to deliver results for our clients.

Our teams are inclusive and composed of individuals from different geographies, cultures, religions, ethnicities, races, genders, sexual orientations, abilities and generations.

We invest in great leaders who bring out the best in you and the company, enabling us to multiply our impact and results. This is why, year after year, we are recognized worldwide as a great place to work.

Gartner is the world authority on AI

At Gartner, you’ll join a company at the very center of the AI revolution. Gartner has proactive, objective guidance throughout clients’ AI journeys. We set the standard for how organizations leverage artificial intelligence to drive meaningful impact. You’ll have access to unmatched resources, expertise, and technology, and play a key role in helping Gartner and our clients innovate and grow as we leverage AI to transform business and technology landscapes.

It’s an exciting time to be at Gartner, with limitless opportunities to make a real impact, grow your skills, and build a lasting, meaningful career in a field that’s reshaping the way we operate. If you’re passionate about AI and want to be part of a team that’s guiding the leaders who shape the world, Gartner is the place for you.

What do we offer?

Gartner offers world-class benefits, highly competitive compensation and disproportionate rewards for top performers.

In our hybrid work environment, we provide the flexibility and support for you to thrive — working virtually when it's productive to do so and getting together with colleagues in a vibrant community that is purposeful, engaging and inspiring.

Ready to grow your career with Gartner? Join us.

Gartner believes in fair and equitable pay. A reasonable estimate of the base salary range for this role is 188,000 USD - 225,000 USD. Please note that actual salaries may vary within the range, or be above or below the range, based on factors including, but not limited to, education, training, experience, professional achievement, business need, and location. Ziply Fiber is a local internet service provider dedicated to elevating the connected lives of the communities we serve. We offer the fastest home internet in the nation, a refreshingly great customer experience, and affordable plans that put customers in charge.

As our state-of-the-art fiber network expands, so does our need for team members who can help us grow and realize our goals.

Our Company Values:

  • Genuinely Caring:We treat customers and colleagues like neighbors, with empathy and full attention.
  • Empowering You:We help customers choose what is best for them, and we support employees in implementing new ideas and solutions.
  • Innovation and Improvement:We constantly seek ways to improve how we serve customers and each other.
  • Earning Your Trust:We build trust through clear, honest, human communication.

Job Summary

Internet performance is a competitive differentiator for Ziply Fiber, and the Principal Architect for IPAM, Peering & Caching owns three of the most direct levers: how efficiently we manage our IP address space, how well we position ourselves in the peering ecosystem, and how effectively we cache the content our subscribers want. The Principal Architect will define Ziply Fiber's IP address management architecture, build out our Internet Exchange presence and peering relationships, and design the content caching strategy that reduces transit costs while delivering the fastest possible experience to our subscribers.

Reporting to the VP, Network Architecture & Engineering, this role serves as the senior architecture authority for IP address management, peering, transit strategy, Internet Exchange participation, routing security, and content-delivery optimization.

This is a senior independent contributor role that leads through technical expertise, architecture governance, standards ownership, and cross-functional influence rather than direct people-management responsibility.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

The Essential Duties and Responsibilities listed below are a range of duties performed by the employee and not intended to reflect all duties performed.

IP Address Management

●Own the enterprise IPAM architecture: tooling selection (NetBox, Infoblox, or equivalent), IPv4/IPv6 address plan design, allocation policy, and lifecycle management.

●Define IPv4 conservation strategy: efficient allocation, reclamation workflows, and planning for long-term IPv4 exhaustion in a dual-stack and IPv6-only transition context.

●Architect IPv6 address plan: PA vs. PI space strategy, allocation hierarchy, and delegation policy for residential, business, and infrastructure use cases.

●Own RPKI/ROA deployment: route origin authorization strategy, ROA publication, and BGP route validation policy to protect Ziply's routing security posture.

●Maintain authoritative IP registry documentation and integration with provisioning, DNS, and network management systems.

Peering & Transit

●Define and execute Ziply's peering strategy: public and private peering policy, Internet Exchange presence (SIX, PAIX, Equinix IX, or equivalent), and route optimization.

●Own transit provider architecture: provider selection, diversity standards, failover policy, and commercial alignment with traffic growth forecasts.

●Manage peering relationships: technical onboarding, LOA management, route object maintenance (ARIN, IRR), and ongoing relationship health.

●Analyze traffic matrices and peering economics to identify new peering opportunities, optimize routing, and reduce transit spend.

●Coordinate with IP Core & Metro architect on BGP policy implementation and route propagation standards.

Content Caching

●Design and own Ziply's content caching strategy: placement of embedded caches (Netflix OCA, Google GGC, Meta, Apple, Akamai, or equivalent) within the network to maximize cache hit rates and minimize transit egress.

●Define cache node placement criteria: subscriber density, traffic volume thresholds, and co-location requirements for each CDN partner.

●Manage CDN partner relationships: technical integration, cache performance monitoring, and capacity scaling agreements.

●Analyze CDN traffic reports and cache efficiency metrics to continuously optimize placement and configuration.

●Coordinate with Network Planning and IP Core teams to ensure caching infrastructure is reflected in capacity planning models.

Other Duties

·Performs other duties as required to support the business and evolving organization.

Required Qualifications:

·High school diploma or GED.

·Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, Telecommunications, Network Engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and directly relevant IP networking, peering, Internet infrastructure, transit, routing, CDN, or architecture experience.

·10+ years of IP network engineering at an internet service provider (ISP) or broadband operator with direct ownership of IPAM, peering, and/or content caching programs.

·Demonstrated senior independent contributor experience setting technical standards, influencing architecture direction, mentoring engineers, and driving cross-functional architecture decisions without direct people-management responsibility.

·Expert-level BGP knowledge: peering policy, community design, route filtering, RPKI/ROA, and traffic engineering at IX scale.

·Hands-on IPAM platform experience: NetBox, Infoblox, or equivalent — including IPv4/IPv6 address plan design and integration with network management systems.

·Experience developing IPAM governance processes, address allocation standards, reclamation workflows, authoritative data-quality controls, and operational reporting for IPv4 and IPv6 environments.

·Deep understanding of CDN caching architectures: embedded cache program requirements for major CDN providers (Netflix, Google, Meta, Akamai, or equivalent) and cache performance optimization.

·Strong peering ecosystem knowledge: IX operations, route object management (IRR, ARIN), LOA workflows, and peering economics.

·Experience with RPKI/ROA deployment and BGP route origin validation.

·Ability to communicate complex peering, routing, IPAM, transit, CDN caching, routing-security, and Internet-performance concepts to executive, technical, operational, vendor, and non-technical audiences

Preferred Qualifications:

●Experience with traffic engineering tools: RIPE STAT, PeeringDB, or IX traffic analytics platforms.

●Familiarity with DNS anycast architecture for resolver infrastructure.

●Background in transit cost optimization and peering business case development.

●JNCIE-SP, CCIE-SP, or equivalent certification.

●Experience presenting peering, transit, caching, Internet-performance, or routing-security strategy to VP-level or executive audiences.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

·Ability to work independently and apply sound judgment and reasoning skills to a variety of situations.

·Ability to multi-task and collaborate effectively with other personnel to meet deadlines.

·Strong verbal and written communication, attention to detail, and organizational skills.

·Ability to work within critical deadlines.

·Ability to adjust to rapidly changing priorities and schedules.

·Ability to provide excellent customer service.

·Senior technical leadership skills with the ability to influence Internet architecture, routing policy, IPAM governance, peering strategy, and content-delivery decisions without direct people-management authority.

·Strong analytical and systems-thinking skills with the ability to balance routing resiliency, Internet performance, peering economics, IP address utilization, cache efficiency, customer experience, operational risk, and cost.

·Executive presence and communication skills to explain complex IPAM, peering, transit, RPKI/ROA, CDN caching, and Internet-performance decisions clearly and credibly to Technology, Operations, Finance, Legal, vendors, and senior leadership.

Work Authorization

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the US for any employer. Sponsorship is not available for this position.

Physical Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Essential and marginal functions may require maintaining physical condition necessary for bending, stooping, sitting, walking, or standing for prolonged periods of time; most of time is spent sitting in a comfortable position with frequent opportunity to move about. Work Environment

WHAT THE ROLE OWNS

Design craft

AI production capability

  2. Speed ofoutput. Using AI to compress what used to take a week into a day.
  3. Reusable systems. Turning one-offassets into workﬂows the wider team can run.

The design is the reason it works. The AI is the reason there is so much of it.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Design, end to end

  • Own concept through to shipped asset. Direction, copy, design, build, iterate.
  • Hold a high bar. Enterprise-grade, brand-safe, considered. AI-made should never mean AI-looking, and you are the person who makes sure it never does.

Web and landing pages

  • Design and build campaign, brand and pitch pages with AI at every step.
  • Get a v1 up fast, put it in front ofthe CEO and sales, iterate live rather than polishing in private.

Presentations and collateral

  • Build decks and proposals for named enterprise opportunities at short notice, going from direction to draft in hours rather than days.
  • Turn a rough direction from the CEO or a sales lead into a ﬁnished, on-brand asset.

Use AI to close the gaps rather than waiting for a perfect brief.

  • Keep the collateral library current so everything we send looks like it came from one company.

Across marketing

  • Work wherever the marketing need is. Campaigns, social, web, brand, product marketing, events, outbound.
  • Write as well as design. AI gets you most ofthe way, your judgement gets it the rest.
  • Sit close to sales so you can see which assets convert and which do not, and adjust accordingly.

AI-ﬁrst production

  • Use AI across every step. Ideation, copy, design, build, iteration, QA.
  • Find the manual steps in how we produce work and replace them.
  • Bring newAI tools, models and techniques to the CEO before we hear about them elsewhere. Part ofthe value ofthis role is that you are living at the AI frontier.

Working with the CEO

  • Short feedback loops, direct access, no committee.
  • Be highly responsive. Messages get answered, work moves, momentum is the point.

WHO YOU ARE

A designer ﬁrst

  • You have real design depth. Typography, layout, hierarchy, colour, grid, motion. You know the rules well enough to break them on purpose.
  • Your portfolio is strong and you can talk through the thinking behind it, not just the output.

  • Fluent in the traditional tooling. Figma, Adobe, whatever you use to get from idea to ﬁnished thing.
  • You have taste and you can defend it. You can explain why one approach beats another in terms a marketing lead will accept.

AI-native

  • You have restructured how you work around AI, not bolted it on. You can walk us through your workﬂows, your tools and your output.
  • You are comfortable letting AI do the parts that used to take days, and conﬁdent about which parts still need you.

How you operate

  • A maker. Hands-on, not a manager ofpeople who make things.
  • A fast, clear writer. Direction gets acknowledged, questions get asked early rather than late, progress is visible without anyone having to ask.
  • Organised and structured. Requirements arrive from across the business and they rarely arrive tidy. You triage them, sequence them against commercial priority, and keep a clear picture ofwhat is landing when. Nothing gets dropped and you do not need to be chased.
  • Relentless energy. You would rather ship ﬁve things this week than perfect one thing next month.
  • Speed wins and you know it. You treat turnaround time as a feature ofthe work, not a constraint on it.
  • Commercially aware. This work exists to win revenue and you judge it on that basis.

Useful, not essential

  • Understanding ofvideo production
  • Video editing

  • SEO

We care far more about what you have shipped than where you studied.

Growth Strategist

About the Role
We are looking for an exceptional Growth Strategist to join our Growth team. This is one of the most senior strategic roles within FINN Partners and is suited to an experienced agency strategist with deep research expertise and the judgment to turn findings into clear, actionable strategy. Research is the foundation of this role, and it exists to drive decisions. This person will move fluidly across primary and secondary research, digital and social listening, and AI-enabled methods, using whichever combination best answers the question at hand, and will translate what they learn into insight that reframes how clients see their business, audience, market, or competition. From there, they will make clear strategic recommendations, working closely with specialists across the agency to ensure those recommendations are realistic and implementable.
While the role sits within the Growth team and plays a critical part in winning new business, it extends beyond RFPs and pitches. This person will also provide strategic and research leadership on existing client accounts, including engagements they were not involved in winning.

The role requires intellectual curiosity, strong research capability, commercial judgment, and the confidence to make clear recommendations often with limited information and tight deadlines.

Responsibilities
Research & Insight
  • Lead the design and execution of research across methodologies choosing the right mix for the question, timeline, and budget at hand.
  • Shape research methodology around the business question and the strategic decisions the client needs to make.
  • Move quickly and resourcefully in new business contexts without compromising the credibility of the findings.
  • Develop surveys, questionnaires, sampling approaches, and analytical frameworks when primary research is warranted.
  • Personally conduct executive stakeholder interviews, customer interviews, and other in-depth qualitative research.
  • Analyze findings alongside market, audience, competitor, and performance data.
  • Translate findings into insight that drives a decision: what the evidence says, why it matters, and what the client or FINN should do next.
  • Work effectively with specialist researchers, analysts, and external vendors while maintaining strategic ownership of the engagement.
  • Develop segmentation models, personas, journeys, and messaging frameworks that can be used and defended in front of senior leadership.
  • Maintain a working knowledge of evolving industry landscapes, methodologies, and cultural trends so recommendations stay current.
Strategy & Growth
  • Lead the strategic development of new business opportunities and RFP responses, using research to identify the central business challenge and build the case for why FINN is the right partner.
  • Develop insight-led strategies that differentiate FINN's proposals and create competitive advantage.
  • Translate research and strategy into practical recommendations that client and agency teams can implement.
  • Collaborate with creative, digital, PR, media, and account teams to ensure recommendations are realistic and well-supported.
  • Present strategic recommendations to prospective clients and senior FINN leadership.
  • Build measurement frameworks and KPIs aligned with client objectives.
  • Remain engaged following successful pitches to preserve continuity and support implementation.
  • Manage multiple opportunities and engagements simultaneously, balancing competing priorities and deadlines.
Client Leadership
  • Serve as a trusted research and strategy adviser to senior clients.
  • Provide strategic leadership on existing client accounts, including those where you were not involved in the original pitch.
  • Quickly get up to speed on unfamiliar businesses, industries, and operating environments.
  • Communicate complex findings and recommendations clearly and confidently, earning stakeholder buy-in through the credibility and rigor of the work rather than force of personality.
  • Identify opportunities to grow existing client relationships through additional research or strategic consulting.

Skills & Experience

The successful candidate will have:
  • Minimum 15 years of strategic experience, with the majority gained in an agency or consulting environment.
  • Significant experience designing and leading research across a range of methodologies.
  • Strong judgment about data quality and rigor, balanced with the scrappiness to move fast when new business timelines demand it.
  • Strong knowledge of survey design, sampling, research methodology, analysis, and insight development.
  • Experience personally conducting executive, stakeholder, and customer interviews.
  • Proven track record leading strategy for complex pitches, RFPs, and new business opportunities.
  • Ability to synthesize large volumes of information into a clear strategic point of view.
  • Excellent strategic storytelling, presentation, and facilitation skills, grounded in command of the evidence and the ability to defend a recommendation under scrutiny.
  • A track record of earning the confidence of senior stakeholders through the quality and credibility of their work.
  • A strong point of view on where marketing, media, and culture are heading.
  • Strong commercial acumen and the ability to connect research and strategy to measurable business outcomes.
  • Comfort working with ambiguity, limited information, and evolving client requirements.
Personal Attributes
The ideal candidate will be:
  • Intellectually curious and insight driven.
  • Methodologically flexible and resourceful, with good instincts for when data is solid enough to act on.
  • Decisive, with the judgment to make a clear recommendation rather than present a list of options.
  • Commercially minded and focused on business outcomes.
  • Confident and credible in the room, earning trust through command of the work rather than salesmanship.
  • Structured and analytical, without losing sight of the bigger picture.
  • Comfortable navigating ambiguity and incomplete information.
  • Proactive and self-directed.
  • Passionate about solving complex business and growth challenges.
Success in This Role
Success will be measured by the ability to:
  • Win new business through differentiated, research-backed strategic thinking.
  • Lead credible research that uncovers meaningful business and audience opportunities.
  • Translate research into decisions clients act on and business FINN wins.
  • Build trusted relationships with senior stakeholders.
  • Grow existing client relationships through valuable strategic consulting.
  • Create measurable business impact for FINN and its clients.

Anticipated Salary:
$150,000 - $200,000
Commensurate with experience and depending upon the workplace.

Please upload your resume and cover letter, along with your desired salary in $USD.
While we appreciate the interest of all applicants, we will only respond to those whose qualifications closely align with the role.
About FINN Partners:
FINN Partners is a global integrated marketing agency recognized as a top employer and an award-winning workplace. We are entrepreneurial, collaborative, and committed to shaping a bold future with clients across technology, healthcare, education, travel, and more. We celebrate creativity, curiosity, and the pursuit of meaningful, impactful work.

Join us to be part of an agency that works hard, plays nice, and always strives for excellence.

Impinj is a leading RAIN RFID provider and Internet of Things pioneer. Team Overview:

The RAIN Reader IC (RIC) design group is part of the Impinj Silicon Engineering department and is responsible for the development of Impinj’s RIC products. Within the RIC Design group, the digital team owns the digital subsystems of these products, including the digital modem, the microcontroller subsystem, digital control loops, calibration engines, and the control and interface logic for analog IP. The team carries these designs from architecture and micro-architecture definition through RTL, verification, DFT, and timing closure to tapeout, post-silicon bring-up, and validation, partnering closely with chip architects, RF/analog designers, physical design, and CAD/EDA engineers and using state-of-the-art tools and methodologies. The team works to balance short-term goals needed to deliver products rapidly to market and long-term enhancements to methodologies and practices to enable future efficiencies.

What You'll Do:

  • Drive the digital design of Impinj's next-generation RAIN RFID Reader ICs from architecture through tapeout and silicon validation.
  • Develop micro-architectures, create executable models, and implement RTL for complex digital and mixed-signal IC subsystems.
  • Collaborate with chip architects and RF/analog engineers to partition and realize advanced mixed-signal architectures, including digital control loops, calibration engines, and interface logic for analog IP.
  • Partner with physical design and verification teams to ensure timing closure, signal integrity, and delivery of production-ready Reader ICs.
  • Define and implement DFT strategies — including scan insertion, BIST, and boundary scan — appropriate for mixed-signal Reader IC designs.
  • Work with CAD/EDA engineers to evolve Impinj's ASIC/SoC design flows, methodologies, and best practices.
  • Enhance existing RAIN RFID Reader products with new features, performance improvements, and power optimizations.
  • Support post-silicon bring-up and debug, correlating RTL and simulation results with lab measurements to validate design intent.

What You'll Bring:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, with 12 years of experience (or 8 years with MS or 5 years with a PhD) required.
  • 12+ years of RTL design experience, including at least 2–3 full tapeout cycles preferably on mixed-signal or RF-integrated ICs.
  • Strong skills in digital logic design, micro-architecture definition, synthesis, and timing closure.
  • Proficiency in Verilog and SystemVerilog for RTL development, behavioral modeling, and verification.

Scope of Job: ISO Compliance Specialist oversees regulatory compliance for all U.S. independent system operators and regional transmission organizations. An Independent System Operator (ISO) is a neutral, federally regulated organization that coordinates, controls, and monitors the operation of the electrical power system within a single state or region. The primary focus is ERCOT, though the role covers PJM, MISO, CAISO, SPP, NYISO, and ISO-NE. This fully remote position requires expertise in market rules and protocols to ensure company compliance across multiple ISO/RTO markets.

Responsibilities

  • Serves as the company’s primary subject matter expert for ERCOT compliance, including nodal protocols, operating procedures, settlement processes, and market guides.
  • Tracks and reports rule changes in all U.S. ISO/RTO markets, focusing on ERCOT; evaluate business effects of PRRs and stakeholder developments.
  • Develops and maintains internal compliance policies, procedures, and controls tailored to each ISO/RTO in which the company participates.
  • Conducts regular internal audits and gap analyses across trading, scheduling, settlements, and operations functions for multi-market compliance exposure.
  • Manages all required filings, notifications, and reports to ERCOT, PUCT, FERC, and other applicable regulatory bodies on time and with accuracy.
  • Serves as primary liaison for ERCOT Market Surveillance, PUCT enforcement inquiries, and NERC/Regional Entity audit activities.
  • Coordinates cross-market compliance calendars and risk registers, ensuring obligations across all ISO/RTO footprints are tracked and met.
  • Designs and delivers compliance training programs for operational, trading, and scheduling staff across all relevant markets.
  • Collaborates with legal, finance, and operations teams to embed compliance requirements into new market strategies, products, and systems.
  • Participates in ISO/RTO stakeholder meetings and working groups, particularly within ERCOT, representing the company’s interests in rulemaking processes.
  • Prepares executive-level compliance reporting and escalate material risks to leadership in a clear, timely manner. Other duties as assigned.

Supervision of Others: No direct supervisory duties. Will need to manage consultants and contractors when needed

Working Conditions:

95% of time is spent in the office environment utilizing computers (frequent use of various Microsoft software/programs), phones, and general office equipment. 5% of time is spent outside of the office visiting vendors’ and/or internal customers’ sites in addition to attending various conferences and meetings.

Qualifications

Education/Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree required, master’s degree preferred.
  • 5+ years of regulatory compliance experience within U.S. ISO/RTO wholesale energy markets, with demonstrated ERCOT expertise as a primary requirement.
  • Experience with PUCT regulations and the Texas wholesale and retail energy market structure.

Skills/Knowledge/Abilities:

  • In-depth knowledge of ERCOT nodal protocols, market rules, QSE/LSE obligations, ancillary services, and settlement processes.
  • Working knowledge of at least one additional ISO/RTO (PJM, MISO, CAISO, SPP, NYISO, or ISO-NE) market rules and compliance frameworks.
  • Familiarity with applicable NERC Reliability Standards (FAC, BAL, IRO, TOP, COM, and related series) and their applicability to generation, transmission, and market participants.
  • Hands-on experience responding to ERCOT enforcement inquiries and preparing mitigation plans.
  • Multi-ISO/RTO compliance experience across two or more markets simultaneously.
  • Familiarity with ERCOT’s nodal settlement system.
  • Experience using compliance management tools.
  • Proven ability to manage multi-market compliance workstreams independently in a remote, fast-paced environment.
  • Strong analytical, documentation, and organizational skills with exceptional attention to regulatory detail.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills; comfortable translating complex regulatory requirements for non-technical audiences.
  • Ability to work effectively as a self-directed remote employee, with strong time management and virtual collaboration skills.

Physical Requirements:

Must be able to sit or stand at computer for a reasonable length of time typing and reading. Regularly required to walk or stand. 100% of time is spent in the office environment, utilizing computers (frequent use of various Microsoft software/programs), phones, and general office equipment.

Join the Tilt team

At Tilt, we see a side of people that traditional lenders miss. Our mobile-first products and machine learning-powered credit models look beyond credit scores, using over 250 real-time financial signals to recognize real potential. With millions of customers worldwide, we're not just changing how people access financial products — we're creating a new credit system that backs the working, whatever they're working toward.


The Opportunity: Senior Credit Manager, US Core

Tilt is looking for a Senior Manager to support our Cash Advance business, one of our largest and most established product lines. You'll work at the intersection of credit policy, model development, and product strategy, helping us maintain the rigor and velocity of our existing credit programs while supporting a growing agenda of new product experimentation. This is an individual-contributor role with outsized visibility: you won't manage a team, but you will regularly partner with and influence senior leaders and cross-functional stakeholders across the business.

This role is a great fit for someone who wants deep ownership of high-impact analytical work and who's energized by moving between rigorous quantitative analysis and creative, ambiguous conceptual problems.


How You'll Make an Impact

  • Sustain credit model and policy velocity: Support the ongoing development and refinement of credit models and underwriting policies for Cash Advance, helping maintain quality and pace as the program evolves.

  • Drive new product experimentation: Partner on the design and evaluation of new product constructs and pricing approaches, bringing rigorous credit analysis to test-and-learn initiatives that are still taking shape.

  • Bridge new product experiences and credit rigor: Bring both a user/product lens and a quantitative credit policy lens to new initiatives — helping ideas move from concept to tested, scalable strategy.

  • Communicate with precision and influence: Translate complex analysis into clear, decision-ready recommendations for senior stakeholders, and build the credibility to shape decisions without formal authority.

  • Partner cross-functionally: Work closely with data science, product, marketing and other credit and risk functions to keep initiatives moving and aligned with the broader business strategy.

  • Bring creativity and structure to ambiguous problems: Help scope and structure new analytical questions where the path isn't yet defined, and move initiatives forward with urgency and independent judgment.


Why You're a Great Fit

  • Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field (Engineering, Business, Finance, Computer Science, Mathematics, Economics, or similar); advanced degree a plus.

  • 5-7 years of experience in credit risk, data analytics, or a related quantitative discipline, ideally in consumer lending or fintech.

  • Excellent communication skills — able to go deep in the analytical weeds and also distill findings clearly for an executive audience.

  • Demonstrated ability to influence outcomes and build trust with senior stakeholders and cross-functional partners without formal reporting authority.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving instincts, with comfort operating in ambiguity and a track record of driving projects forward independently.

  • A creative, action-oriented approach — someone who prototypes, tests, and iterates rather than waiting for a fully-defined brief.

  • Eagerness to learn new tools and methods, and to stay current with trends in credit, lending, and AI.

Don’t meet every qualification? We care about potential over your past. If you're bringing ambition and drive to what we're building, we want to hear from you.

What you'll get at Tilt

  • Virtual-first teamwork: The Tilt team is collaborating across 14 countries, 12 time zones, and counting. You’ll get started with a WFH office reimbursement.

  • Competitive pay: We're big on potential, and it's reflected in our competitive compensation packages and generous equity.

  • Complete support: Find flexible health plans at every premium level, and substantial subsidies that stand up to global standards.

  • Visibility is yours: You can count on direct exposure to our leadership team — we’re a team where good ideas travel quickly.

  • Paid global onsites: Magic happens IRL: we gather twice yearly to reconnect over shared meals or kayaking adventures. (We’ve visited Vail, San Diego, and Mexico City, to name a few.)

  • Impact is recognized: Growth opportunities follow your contributions, not rigid promotion timelines.

The Tilt Way

We're looking for people who chase excellence and impact. Those who stand behind their work, celebrating the wins and learning from the missteps equally. We foster an environment where every voice is valued and mutual respect is non-negotiable — brilliant jerks need not apply. We're in this together, working to expand access to fair credit and prove that people are incredible. When you join us, it's not just another day at the [virtual] office, you're helping millions of hardworking people reach better financial futures.

You’re pushing ahead in your career? We can get behind that. Join us in building the credit system that people deserve.

jobs.description:
ISP Network Support Engineer (BGP, MikroTik, Peplink, SD-WAN & Wireless) – Remote | U.S. Hours

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S. Business Hours
On-Call: Rotating after-hours emergency support — approximately 1 week per month

About the Role

At Pavago, we’re hiring an ISP Network Support Engineer for one of our clients to support customer-facing troubleshooting and production network operations across a growing multi-WAN ISP environment.

This is not a basic helpdesk role. You’ll work directly with live network infrastructure across fiber, fixed wireless, bonded WAN, Starlink, and SD-WAN deployments, troubleshooting complex connectivity issues and maintaining reliable, high-availability services.

You’ll work hands-on with technologies including MikroTik RouterOS, Peplink SpeedFusion, BGP, OSPF, Cambium, Ubiquiti, Siklu, Aviat, and enterprise wireless infrastructure.

This role is particularly well suited to someone with hands-on ISP, WISP, FTTH, or MSP experience who is comfortable troubleshooting production networks while communicating directly with customers.

What You’ll Own

Customer Network Support & Troubleshooting

  • Diagnose customer issues involving:
    • Connectivity and outages
    • Latency and packet loss
    • Routing instability
    • VoIP and call-quality problems
    • WAN and failover performance
  • Troubleshoot bonded WAN, SD-WAN, VPN, VLAN, and wireless connectivity issues.
  • Support routers, firewalls, and Customer Premise Equipment (CPE).
  • Investigate issues across multiple layers rather than simply escalating tickets.
  • Document troubleshooting steps, root causes, and configuration changes.
  • Communicate technical findings clearly to business customers.
  • Advise customers on redundancy, failover, and network optimization.
  • Participate in rotating after-hours emergency support.

ISP Network Operations

  • Monitor and maintain:
    • Edge routing infrastructure
    • Wireless backhaul systems
    • Bonded WAN infrastructure
    • Core ISP services
  • Provision and configure customer network deployments.
  • Configure:
    • Routers
    • VLANs
    • Firewall rules
    • NAT
    • QoS
    • VPNs
  • Diagnose BGP and OSPF routing issues, routing loops, WAN instability, and failover events.
  • Maintain configuration backups, firmware updates, IP documentation, and network hardening standards.

MikroTik, Peplink & SD-WAN

  • Configure and troubleshoot MikroTik RouterOS environments.
  • Support Peplink SpeedFusion and InControl2.
  • Troubleshoot multi-WAN bonding and failover behavior.
  • Support hybrid connectivity involving:
    • Fiber
    • Fixed wireless
    • Starlink
    • 5G
    • Terrestrial WAN connections
  • Optimize redundancy and high-availability configurations.

Fixed Wireless & Backhaul Infrastructure

  • Support fixed wireless environments using:
    • Cambium
    • Ubiquiti
    • PTP/PMP architectures
  • Work with high-capacity wireless backhaul technologies including:
    • Siklu
    • Aviat
    • mmWave infrastructure
  • Support tower deployments, backhaul upgrades, and infrastructure expansion.
  • Troubleshoot signal, connectivity, capacity, and backhaul performance issues.

VoIP & QoS

  • Troubleshoot SIP and VoIP quality issues.
  • Diagnose network conditions affecting voice traffic.
  • Configure and optimize QoS policies.
  • Prioritize latency-sensitive traffic appropriately.
  • Help maintain consistent voice quality across multi-WAN environments.

Documentation & Configuration Management

  • Maintain accurate:
    • Network diagrams
    • IP documentation
    • Device configurations
    • Troubleshooting records
    • Configuration backups
  • Document root-cause findings and remediation steps.
  • Keep infrastructure documentation current following network changes.
  • Help reduce repeat incidents through accurate documentation and preventative improvements.

Technical Environment

You may work across:

Routing & Networking

  • MikroTik RouterOS
  • BGP
  • OSPF
  • TCP/IP
  • VLANs
  • NAT
  • QoS
  • VPNs

SD-WAN & Multi-WAN

  • Peplink
  • SpeedFusion
  • InControl2
  • Starlink
  • 5G
  • WAN bonding and failover

Wireless & Backhaul

  • Cambium
  • Ubiquiti
  • Siklu
  • Aviat
  • PTP/PMP
  • mmWave

Enterprise Wi-Fi

  • Cambium cnMaestro
  • UniFi

Voice

  • SIP
  • VoIP
  • QoS and voice optimization

Required Experience & Skills

  • Hands-on networking experience within an ISP, WISP, FTTH, MSP, or similar production network environment.
  • Strong experience troubleshooting:
    • Routing
    • Switching
    • WAN connectivity
    • Network outages
    • Failover systems
  • Hands-on experience configuring:
    • Routers
    • Firewalls
    • VLANs
    • VPNs
  • Strong understanding of:
    • TCP/IP
    • NAT
    • QoS
    • VLANs
    • BGP
    • OSPF
  • Ability to troubleshoot live production networking issues methodically.
  • Strong documentation and root-cause analysis skills.
  • Strong written and verbal English communication.
  • Ability to communicate effectively with both technical teams and customers.
  • Comfortable working independently in a remote environment.
  • Availability for rotating after-hours emergency support.

Strongly Preferred

  • Hands-on MikroTik RouterOS expertise.
  • Experience with Peplink, SpeedFusion, and InControl2.
  • Experience with:
    • Cambium
    • Ubiquiti
    • Siklu
    • Aviat
  • Fixed wireless or WISP deployment experience.
  • PTP/PMP and mmWave backhaul experience.
  • Starlink or hybrid WAN experience.
  • VoIP troubleshooting experience involving:
    • SIP
    • QoS
    • Voice-quality optimization
  • Experience supporting multi-WAN and high-availability network environments.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • You’ve worked on real production networks, not only lab environments.
  • You can troubleshoot complex connectivity problems without immediately escalating them.
  • You understand how routing, WAN links, wireless infrastructure, and failover interact.
  • You remain calm and methodical during outages.
  • You care about uptime, redundancy, and network reliability.
  • You can explain complex network problems clearly to customers.
  • You take ownership of an issue through diagnosis and resolution.
  • You proactively look for ways to prevent repeat incidents.

What a Typical Day Looks Like

Your day may include:

  • Troubleshooting customer connectivity, latency, and routing issues.
  • Investigating BGP/OSPF or multi-WAN failover problems.
  • Configuring MikroTik routers, VLANs, VPNs, firewalls, and QoS.
  • Monitoring wireless backhaul and ISP infrastructure.
  • Provisioning new customer connections.
  • Troubleshooting Peplink SpeedFusion or bonded WAN deployments.
  • Investigating VoIP quality issues.
  • Supporting infrastructure expansions and network upgrades.
  • Updating configuration records and network diagrams.
  • Coordinating with engineering and field teams on escalations.

In short: you help keep production ISP infrastructure stable, scalable, and highly available while solving complex customer and network issues across modern wired, wireless, and SD-WAN environments.

Key Metrics for Success

  • Fast and accurate ticket resolution.
  • High network uptime and reliability.
  • Reduced repeat incidents and escalations.
  • Successful customer provisioning.
  • Effective resolution of routing and failover issues.
  • Accurate network documentation and configuration management.
  • Strong customer satisfaction and communication quality.

Why This Role Stands Out

  • Hands-on exposure to real ISP/WISP production infrastructure.
  • Work directly with BGP, MikroTik, Peplink, SD-WAN, wireless backhaul, and multi-WAN environments.
  • Exposure to modern connectivity technologies including Starlink and hybrid WAN.
  • Strong technical ownership rather than basic Tier 1 support.
  • Opportunity to work across both customer-facing troubleshooting and infrastructure operations.
  • Clear growth opportunities into:
    • Senior Network Engineer
    • ISP Network Engineer
    • Infrastructure Engineer
    • Network Operations Lead
    • Network Architect

Interview Process

  • Initial Screening Call
  • Technical Interview
  • Practical Network Troubleshooting Scenario
  • Final Interview

jobs.title: Virtual Financial Aid Disbursements and R2T4 Specialist, FAME
jobs.excerpt: Who we areAt Aquila, we invest in category-defining B2B/B2G software companies globally, acting as a thought-partner, striving for the success of our companies in the long term.
jobs.description:
Who we are

At Aquila, we invest in category-defining B2B/B2G software companies globally, acting as a thought-partner, striving for the success of our companies in the long term. We are a well-managed, profitable company that operates like a startup with the financial backing of a parent company. For our people, this means limitless possibilities.

We are unapologetically unique, pivoting to respond to the needs of the multiple markets we operate in. We have ambitious goals, and we are looking for genuine contributors with integrity, energy, flexibility, and loyalty. We are investing in building future leaders who can take an idea and make things happen.

Who we need

For over 45 years, Fame has been a trusted partner to post-secondary schools. We recognize the challenges that career school administrators face in managing their institutions, from streamlining operations to ensuring regulatory compliance. At Fame, we provide the support and tools needed to navigate these complexities and run academic institutions efficiently. Our student information systems, supporting tools, and Admission CRM Software, including powerful EDlumina, help simplify and streamline these processes.

Reporting to the Virtual Financial Aid Disbursement and Drops Team Lead, we are hiring a Virtual Financial Aid Disbursements and R2T4 Specialist to join our Virtual Financial Aid Office. As our new Virtual Financial Aid Disbursements and R2T4 Specialist, you will play a critical role in ensuring federal student aid is processed accurately, compliantly, and on time for the schools we support. You will manage financial aid disbursements, Return to Title IV (R2T4) calculations, refunds, and related processes while partnering with school administrators to resolve day-to-day financial aid questions and maintain compliance with federal regulations. Working across multiple systems and supporting a portfolio of assigned schools, you will help ensure financial aid operations run smoothly through careful auditing, attention to detail, and a commitment to accuracy.

This is a remote role open to candidates anywhere in the United States. While candidates in any U.S. time zone are welcome to apply, working hours should align primarily with the Eastern Time zone.

Who you are

You have experience working in financial aid administration and understand the importance of accuracy, compliance, and attention to detail when managing federal student aid. You are process-driven and organized, with the ability to manage competing priorities while consistently producing high-quality work. You naturally catch errors, ask questions when something doesn't seem right, and take ownership of your work. Whether collaborating with school administrators or supporting colleagues, you communicate clearly, build trusted relationships, and are equally comfortable working independently and as part of a remote team.

What’s in it for you

Meaningful impact. Behind every disbursement, refund, and compliance check is a student relying on financial aid to continue their education. Your work will help schools administer federal aid accurately and efficiently, ensuring students receive the support they need while maintaining compliance with complex regulations.

Develop your expertise. You will join a team that values learning and sets you up for success through structured onboarding, hands-on shadowing, and ongoing collaboration. As you build confidence across disbursements, Return to Title IV calculations, and financial aid operations, you will deepen your expertise in a highly specialized area of higher education administration.

A collaborative remote team. Although you will independently manage a portfolio of schools, you will never work in isolation. You will be part of a close-knit, cross-trained team that shares knowledge, supports one another, and works together to ensure consistent service and coverage for every client school.

How you will make an impact:

  • Ensure timely and accurate financial aid disbursements. You will process federal Title IV aid disbursements, ensuring funds are released accurately, on schedule, and in compliance with federal regulations and school requirements. Through careful review and attention to detail, you will help ensure students receive the financial support they are entitled to while maintaining the integrity of the financial aid process.
  • Manage withdrawals and refund processing. You will perform Return to Title IV (R2T4) and institutional refund calculations, process student withdrawals, and ensure all required documentation and reporting are completed accurately. Your work will help schools remain compliant while supporting students through changes in their enrollment.
  • Partner with schools to support day-to-day operations. You will serve as a trusted resource for your assigned schools, responding to questions, providing guidance on financial aid processes, and helping resolve operational issues. By building strong relationships and delivering responsive support, you will contribute to a seamless financial aid experience for school administrators and students.
  • Maintain quality and compliance. You will audit your work, identify discrepancies, and ensure financial aid records remain complete, accurate, and aligned with regulatory requirements. Working across systems including FAME, COD, and internal tools, you will help protect compliance while supporting efficient financial aid operations.
  • Collaborate and continuously improve. You will work closely with your team to share knowledge, provide coverage across assigned schools, and contribute to process improvements. As regulations and operational needs evolve, you will embrace new learning opportunities and help strengthen the consistency and quality of the services we provide.

Here’s what you bring:

  • The financial aid expertise. You have experience administering federal financial aid and a strong understanding of Title IV regulations, including disbursements, Return to Title IV (R2T4) calculations, and refund processing. You are confident in interpreting regulatory requirements and applying them accurately in a fast-paced environment.
  • The technical skills. You are comfortable working across financial aid and student information systems to manage complex processes and maintain accurate records. Experience with FAME software, COD, NSLDS, or similar financial aid platforms is highly valued, and you are confident in learning new technologies and navigating multiple systems simultaneously.
  • The attention to detail. You take pride in producing accurate work and have a disciplined approach to reviewing, auditing, and validating information before it is finalized. You can manage multiple priorities without compromising quality and recognize the importance of precision in a highly regulated environment.
  • The communication skills. You build positive working relationships with school administrators, colleagues, and, when needed, students and families. You communicate clearly, explain complex information in an approachable way, and are committed to providing responsive, professional service.
  • The mindset. You are self-motivated, curious, and comfortable working independently in a remote environment while knowing when to ask questions or seek guidance. You enjoy collaborating with others, embrace opportunities to learn, and contribute to a team that values accuracy, accountability, and shared success.

Why join?

Aquila is a division of Constellation Software Inc., one of the largest and most successful software companies in Canada and the most successful technology stock in Canada over the last 10 years [TSE: CSU].

Our entrepreneurial culture, lean environment, and people come together to form a dynamic organization where purpose drives our growth. This is a place where high performance and hard work are rewarded, where leaders are grown, and where the best ideas win. With the autonomy to be creative and curious, we collaborate and iterate to achieve real impact in the communities we support.

We spend our days asking questions and challenging the status quo, manipulating our structure, roles, and internal operations in order to stay ahead in a competitive landscape.

If you share our growth mindset, relationship-focused approach, and high moral fiber, you will thrive at Aquila.

Apply now.

Diversity and inclusion are not mere words on paper to us. We welcome and appreciate candidates with a range of backgrounds and experiences. If you have most of the qualifications we are seeking, and want to play an integral role in our success, apply to express your interest.

What you can expect from our interview process:

  • A virtual interview with a Talent Advisor to discuss your interest in joining the company and in the role. The conversation will be recorded using BrightHire, an AI-powered video interview tool. More details will be shared when you are invited to interview.
  • A 45-minute virtual interview with the Virtual Financial Aid Disbursement and Drops Team Lead, focused on your financial aid experience, knowledge of Title IV processes, attention to detail, and approach to supporting schools in a compliant, service-focused environment.

Aquila welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.
